newsitem.title: INDIA: India Ranbaxy hopes to enter US by 1998.
newsitem.headline: India Ranbaxy hopes to enter US by 1998.

text.p: Indian pharmaceutical maker Ranbaxy Laboratories Ltd said on Saturday it hopes to begin marketing its products in the United States by 1998.
"We have approvals pending from the United States," chairman Parvinder Singh told Reuters during a visit to Ranbaxy's research and development centre outside the Indian capital.
"Hopefully we will be getting them in 1997 so that we can maket our products in the United States by 1998," Singh said.
Singh said Ranbaxy, which exports to 45 countries, had recently signed deals to export its products to Egypt, Poland, South Africa and the United Kingdom.
"We are also examining Australia," he said.
He said the Indian pharmaceutical industry was growing at an annual rate of 15 to 16 percent.
"But we are growing at a rate of 20 percent annually," Singh said, referring to Ranbaxy's annual sales.
Ranbaxy's net profit rose to 718 million rupees in the six months up to September 30, 1996, up from 595 million in the same period in 1995.
It recorded sales of 5.1 billion rupees during the first six months of 1996/97 (April-March) against 4.2 billion in the same period in 1995/96.
Ranbaxy recorded export sales of 2.45 billion rupees during April-October 1996 compared to 1.74 billion in the same period in 1995.
The company's current domestic market share is four percent.
